Indigenous Health Assessment (Adults 55 y+)

Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors (e.g., hypertension, diabetes):  
  • Acute central chest pressure with left-arm/shoulder radiation, SOB, diaphoresis, nausea – suspicious for acute coronary syndrome (ACS)  
  • Known hypertension  
  • Smoker (10 cigarettes/day × 15 y)  
  • Overweight (visual assessment; BMI not documented)  
  • Low physical activity  
- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes):  
  • Father died of myocardial infarction at ~60 y  
  • Mother with unspecified “heart problems”  
- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines:  
  Not recorded; patient only reported allergy to aspirin  
- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus):  
  Not recorded  
- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks:  
  Not recorded  
- Lifestyle: physical activity, diet, tobacco, alcohol, substance use:  
  • Physical activity: minimal; “generally don’t do much”  
  • Diet: not recorded  
  • Tobacco: 10 cigarettes/day, 15 y history  
  • Alcohol: 7–8 pints of beer/week  
  • Other substances: none reported  
- Hearing and vision concerns:  
  Not recorded  
- Mood, mental health, and risk assessment (depression, anxiety, self-harm):  
  • Patient anxious/stressed during event; no formal screening completed  
- Social context: family support, caregiving, housing, financial stressors:  
  • Lives alone; no one home at time of call  
  • Owns and works at a sushi restaurant  
  • Door left open for ambulance access  

Examination

- Vital signs: BP, pulse rate and rhythm:  Not recorded  
- Anthropometry: height, weight, BMI, waist circumference if indicated:  Overweight noted visually; exact measurements not recorded  
- Oral health: gums, teeth, dentures if relevant:  Not recorded  
- Ear exam including otoscopy:  Not recorded  
- Eye exam: visual acuity, pupil response, fundus if indicated:  Not recorded  
- Urinalysis: dipstick for protein, glucose, ketones, blood:  Not recorded  

Investigations (as indicated)

- Blood tests: fasting glucose and lipids preferred; HbA1c if diabetes present/suspected:  Not recorded  
- Renal function and liver function tests if clinically indicated:  Not recorded  
- ECG if cardiac risk factors present or baseline:  Ambulance arranged for immediate on-scene ECG  
- Cervical screening if eligible and due:  Not applicable (male)  
- Mammography if eligible and not up to date:  Not applicable  
- Faecal occult blood test if due:  Not recorded  
- Bone density (DEXA) if osteoporosis risk present:  Not recorded  

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings: 60-year-old Indigenous male with hypertension, smoking, overweight, positive family cardiac history, presenting with ongoing central chest pressure radiating to left arm, SOB, diaphoresis, and nausea. First episode; began during light activity. Aspirin allergy (mild swelling).

Working diagnosis: Suspected acute coronary syndrome (myocardial infarction vs. unstable angina). Supported by transcript findings and DDx (high likelihood).

Considerations:  
• Aortic dissection (medium likelihood) – hypertension and smoking; pain character less typical.  
• Pulmonary embolism (low-medium likelihood) – SOB and chest discomfort but risk factors limited.

Management:  
• Emergency ambulance activated; clinician remained on line.  
• Plan for pre-hospital ECG and transport to hospital with cardiac capability.  
• Patient instructed to inform receiving team of aspirin allergy; potential need for antiplatelet therapy despite mild reaction.  
• No other medications given during call.

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification:  Not recorded during emergency call  
- Patient health goals and priorities:  Not recorded  
- Eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA):  Not assessed  
- Referrals (allied health, Quitline, AOD services, Aboriginal health worker, or social supports):  
  • Emergency medical services (ambulance)  
- Follow-up and recall appointments scheduled:  To be determined post-hospital discharge  

Consider

- Mental health support or counselling referral:  mental_health_support_or_not_recorded  
- Specialist referral for complex chronic disease management:  specialist_referral_or_not_recorded (pending hospital findings)  
- Dental referral if oral health issues identified:  Not indicated/not recorded  
- Optometry referral for visual concerns or regular screening:  Not recorded  
- Audiometry referral if hearing issues suspected:  Not recorded  
- Social work or housing support referral if social determinants affect health:  To be assessed after acute event  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Acute coronary syndrome (MI or unstable angina) – High likelihood: classic chest pressure, arm radiation, diaphoresis, nausea, multiple CAD risk factors.  
2. Aortic dissection – Medium likelihood: acute chest pain in hypertensive smoker; pain quality less characteristic, no back radiation noted.  
3. Pulmonary embolism – Low-Medium likelihood: acute SOB and chest discomfort; limited provoking factors and pain non-pleuritic.

Quality checks

● Missing but clinically expected elements: vital signs, BMI, lipid profile, diabetes screening, immunisation review, cancer screening, full medication list.  
● Internal conflicts: none detected between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality notes: clear dialogue; no background noise; limited to emergency context, hence preventive and chronic care details absent.
